name: Algic Family

formality.description: Algic languages express formality through kinship-based respectful address, ceremonial discourse patterns, and elder-directed speech. There is no European-style T-V pronominal distinction. Respectful language is context-dependent rather than pronoun-driven.

gender.inclusiveGuidance: Algic languages use an animacy distinction (animate vs. inanimate noun classes) rather than masculine/feminine grammatical gender. Verbs, demonstratives, quantifiers, and plural markers all agree with the animacy class of their head noun. Animacy assignment is partially arbitrary — some inanimate objects are grammatically animate.

linguisticChallenges.polysynthesis: Algic languages are highly polysynthetic. Verbs carry person markers for both subject and object, plus tense, aspect, mode, and derivational morphemes. A single verb form can express what requires a full clause in English. Word-level MT is fundamentally inadequate for these languages.
linguisticChallenges.animacySystem: The animate/inanimate noun classification triggers agreement throughout the sentence — verbs, demonstratives, and quantifiers all agree with noun animacy. This binary classification system has no parallel in most target languages. Animacy assignment must be memorized per noun.
linguisticChallenges.directInverseVoice: Algic languages use a direct/inverse voice system that marks whether the agent or patient is higher on a person/animacy hierarchy, replacing the active/passive distinction found in European languages. Direct forms are used when the agent outranks the patient; inverse forms when the patient outranks the agent.
linguisticChallenges.obviation: Algic languages have a proximate/obviative distinction for third-person referents — when two third-person entities interact, one is marked as 'proximate' (topical) and the other as 'obviative' (secondary). This discourse-tracking system is typologically rare and routinely mishandled by MT.
linguisticChallenges.headMarking: Algic languages are predominantly head-marking — grammatical relations are marked on the head of a phrase (the verb) rather than on dependents (nouns). This is the opposite of dependent-marking languages like Latin or Turkish.

notes: Family card for Algic (~50 members). This is the broader family containing Algonquian (Cree, Ojibwe, Blackfoot, Mi'kmaq, etc.) plus Yurok and Wiyot. The existing family-algonquian.json card covers the Algonquian branch specifically. This card replaces a previous family-algonquian.json concept at the top-level family position — Algic is the correct top-level family node.
